model_annotation: Both diagrams share the same x-axis, which represents the years from 1995 to 2020 with a linear scale and tick labels at intervals of 5 years. The left diagram has two y-axes: the left y-axis represents the "IWF Fiskalindex" ranging from 0 to 2.5, and the right y-axis represents the "Schuldenquote Gesamtstaat" ranging from 60 to 120. The right diagram also has two y-axes: the left y-axis represents the "IWF Fiskalindex" ranging from -5 to 2, and the right y-axis represents the "Schuldenquote Zentralstaat" ranging from 30 to 70. In the left diagram, two lines are depicted: a blue line representing the "IWF Fiskalindex" with a solid style, starting at approximately 0.1 in 1995, peaking at around 1 in 2008, declining to 0.25 in 2019, and then rising to 0.75 in 2021; and a purple line representing the "Schuldenquote Gesamtstaat" with a solid style, starting at around 60 in 1995, rising to 80 in 2008, and continuing to rise to around 115 in 2021. In the right diagram, two lines are depicted: a blue line representing the "IWF Fiskalindex" with a solid style, starting at around -2 in 1995, increasing to around 0.5 in 2008, declining to -0.5 in 2018, and then rising to 1 in 2021; and a purple line representing the "Schuldenquote Zentralstaat" with a solid style, starting at around 35 in 1995, rising to around 45 in 2005, remaining steady until 2015, and then rising sharply to around 68 in 2021. Blue and red triangles are also present in both diagrams, scattered across the plots without a clear pattern or connection to the lines.
